plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3. This balances winning probability against overpayment risk. My value is $20, so optimal bid ≈ $13.30. Bidding my full value would guarantee zero profit if I win, so shading down is optimal to maximize expected profit.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n times my value, which is (2/3)*29 ≈ 19.33. This balances winning probability against overpaying. Since this is a one-shot game with no prior history, I'll rely on this theoretical optimal bid to maximize expected profit.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is b(v) = v*(n-1)/n = v*2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. For v=45, optimal bid ≈ 30. I'll bid 30 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning against the other two bidders' potentially high values.
